claimBoundary.allowedStatement: The fixed code contains window-wide retrospective decisions, explicit future-data reads, future-conditioned membership logic, and fields that require a dynamic reachability audit.
claimBoundary.forbiddenStatement: Do not claim that suffix information leaks into a deployed model input, changes a benchmark result, or improves a paper table before a real sample mutation reaches the fixed forward path.

staticCodeFindings.finding: The fusion stage derives track length, match counts, association ratios, and cannot_fusion_v2i from the complete fifty-frame observation window, so early rows can depend on later observation rows.
staticCodeFindings.boundary: At the standard prediction cut after frame 49, those rows remain history. This is retrospective smoothing inside the observation window, not prediction-future leakage.

staticCodeFindings.finding: History and future labels coexist in one converted file, but the audited path did not show future coordinates entering historical input tensors.

The actor set uses the first fifty frames, while agent_index is selected from future TARGET_AGENT metadata. Future positions and labels exist in the sample object, but the encoder indexes historical timesteps.
staticCodeFindings.boundary: agent_index is a metadata-reachability suspicion, not a confirmed future-coordinate input.

staticCodeFindings.finding: Future rows generate labels and ref_cetr_idx, while the public loader's model input uses historical feats, masks, and graph data.
staticCodeFindings.boundary: The audited ref_cetr_idx path currently appears to be label or dead metadata.

staticCodeFindings.finding: screen_completed_track requires a future endpoint before an actor is admitted into agent_feature, pred_num, and object_id_lis.
staticCodeFindings.boundary: Future availability controls cohort membership in code, but numerical influence and forward reachability have not been executed.

staticCodeFindings.finding: The default path converts true AV_fut and other_label into planning edges and future-node features.
staticCodeFindings.boundary: This is an explicit oracle design disclosed by the paper, not a newly discovered hidden leak.

staticCodeFindings.finding: The documented entry point, flag semantics, checkpoint spelling, training-mode argument, default paths, and preprocessing schemas contain independent execution blockers.
staticCodeFindings.boundary: A single reachable helper cannot be attributed to a paper result while the public end-to-end path is broken.

partitions: I: tensors, masks, actor ordering, and map edges actually consumed by model forward.
A: fused IDs, source IDs, actor or target selection, interpolated history, and max_source_timestamp provenance.
Y: future labels, metric targets, and loss masks, which are expected to change under suffix mutation.
mutations: Truncate every row after the legal cut and keep labels in a separate sidecar.
Deterministically mutate suffix x, y, velocity, heading, and dimensions.
Permute only suffix id, car_side_id, and road_side_id.
Delete a suffix actor and append an actor that exists only after the cut.
Permute suffix row order as a negative control.
Modify one history row as a positive control.
prefixOracleContract.decisionRule: Canonical I and deployable A must be byte-identical for the same history. A field is a dynamic prefix violation only when its provenance exceeds the legal cut, a suffix mutation changes it, and it reaches the fixed forward path.
prefixOracleContract.closureRule: A crash after suffix truncation is a prefix-closure failure, not automatically a leakage result.
prefixOracleContract.cutRule: The primary V2X-Seq cut is the end of the documented observation window. Earlier cuts require reconstructing an equal-length history ending at that cut.

assetStatus.v2xSeqExample: The official repository publishes a Google Drive TFD example link, but no archive size, hash, local sample, or successful loader run was verified in this environment.
assetStatus.v2xSeqCheckpoints: The official benchmark table links six HiVT and TNT checkpoints on Google Drive. No checkpoint exists in the fixed git tree and none was downloaded, hashed, or loaded.
assetStatus.coMtpCheckpoint: No checkpoint is present; the official checkpoint request remains open at https://github.com/xiaomiaozhang/Co-MTP/issues/4.
assetStatus.licenseBoundary: No independently verified license was found for the relevant TFD data or Co-MTP release. A parent-repository code license must not be projected onto data.
assetStatus.verdict: Assets are link-level public but actual availability, licensing, and fixed-path executability remain unverified; faithful Co-MTP reproduction is hard-blocked.

minimumDynamicStudy.scope: At least 200 cooperative scenes at three legal cuts and at least 1,000 fixed target samples for downstream effects.
baselines: Prefix-only online Hungarian matching with persistent IDs.
An explicit oracle branch as a positive control.
metrics: minADE, minFDE, and miss rate after forward reachability is proven.
minimumDynamicStudy.statistics: Use raw scene or continuous collection segment as the unit. Report exact scene-level binomial intervals, paired cluster bootstrap or cluster sign-flip tests by collection segment or intersection, Holm adjustment for multiple primary metrics, and multiple seeds only when retraining.

killCriteria: No legally usable TFD sample, verifiable checkpoint, or checkpoint-to-preprocessing provenance can be obtained.
At the standard cut, every difference is confined to Y, dead fields, or an explicitly labeled oracle branch while I and fused IDs remain invariant.
The only finding is smoothing within the legal observation history.
Co-MTP preprocessing cannot satisfy the public loader contract without changing its semantics.
The result does not reproduce on independent scenes and a second oracle implementation.
The contribution collapses to a generic slicing-difference utility without a V2X-specific field-level result or reproducible negative certificate.

nearestWorkBoundary.boundary: Baseline-versus-sliced DataFrame leakage detection is established.
Output sensitivity to available history length is established.
Window-before-split time-series leakage is a separate occupied problem.
Truncating the observation window before imputation is an established causal preprocessing principle.
History-timestamp Hungarian and Kalman early fusion already exist; the candidate may audit availability, not reclaim the mechanism.
Temporal ID matching and correction are already proposed; novelty is executable information-boundary auditing.

panelEntryRequirements: TFD sample access and applicable use terms are verified.
At least 200 scenes pass the dynamic suffix-mutation oracle.
Every affected field is traced to model forward or explicitly classified as cohort, label, or dead metadata.
At least one verified checkpoint or an equal-budget runnable predictor completes fixed downstream evaluation.
The novelty statement credits generic lookahead and truncation oracles as prior art.
An independent implementation reproduces the result.
